title: Baseline characteristics of the comparative cohort
verification: canonical numerical checks and publication display checks
caption: Characteristics are described by documented suspected flare status in the eligible cohort. Observed categories use n/evaluable N and percent; missing, Blank, Unknown, and Not applicable categories use n/total group N. Continuous values show the canonical summary and available N, with unavailable counts reported over the total group population. Product, demographics, performance status, prior treatment, cytogenetics, pretreatment disease distribution, marrow involvement, secretion pattern, and baseline laboratory results precede treatment. No hypothesis tests are shown.

title: Management and subsequent course of site-reviewed suspected flare
verification: canonical numerical checks and publication display checks
caption: All site-reviewed cases, the Definite/Probable subset, and Possible cases are shown separately. Each cell uses the total number in its confidence group; unknown assessments remain a separate category. Interventions may overlap. Bispecific treatment action, symptom-resolution status, local lesion outcome, and first post-flare response during the index course are distinct measures. Responses after another systemic therapy are not attributed to the index bispecific course.

title: Structured characteristics of individual site-reviewed cases
verification: canonical numerical checks and publication display checks
caption: Neutral case labels replace original identifiers. Every case value is a predefined code, category, or numeric elapsed value. Chronology uses days after first step-up dosing; timing codes identify recorded points, estimated points, onset intervals, and unavailable timing. Empty numeric entries mean unavailable. First and subsequent response attribution flags, symptom recovery, local lesion outcome, and best index-course systemic response remain distinct. Coded additional-treatment local assessment context identifies radiation, salvage, or CAR-T; NOT_REPORTED does not establish absence of that treatment. Clinical qualification narratives are excluded.

title: Site ascertainment and variable availability
verification: canonical numerical checks and publication display checks
caption: Site-level flare ascertainment and the availability of baseline, response, and survival variables are shown. Courses without recorded flare ascertainment are excluded from the comparative incidence denominator. Availability is specific to each variable and analysis population; missingness is not interpreted as an absent clinical finding.

title: Comparative response and post-treatment events
verification: canonical numerical checks and publication display checks
caption: Full best-response categories, response thresholds, CRS, ICANS, prophylactic and therapeutic tocilizumab, hospital duration, and infections within 30 days are described with their evaluable denominators. Hospital duration uses recorded total days among admitted courses and does not estimate flare-attributable duration. CRS, ICANS, supportive treatment, hospitalization, and infection are post-treatment events; these comparisons do not establish baseline risk or temporal precedence.

title: Baseline laboratory and response association models
verification: canonical numerical checks and publication display checks
caption: All prespecified exploratory Firth logistic models and sensitivity populations are shown with course and patient-cluster counts, flare events, estimates, confidence intervals, and bootstrap diagnostics. Baseline variables are assessed independently for association with documented suspected flare. Adjusted response models use six prespecified baseline covariates. Laboratory tests include Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment. Inference follows the canonical successful-resample threshold and is suppressed when estimation criteria are not met.

title: Time-dependent and landmark survival models
verification: canonical numerical checks and publication display checks
caption: PFS and OS models show exposure-only, corresponding complete-case, and adjusted analyses with population and event counts, confidence intervals, endpoint qualifications, and proportional-hazards diagnostics. Suspected flare becomes an exposure at recorded onset. Sensitivities examine confidence classification, source-supported alternative onset, and day-30/day-60 landmarks. Unknown authoritative endpoints are excluded from affected analyses rather than replaced with conflicting master values. The original-master-endpoint analysis is labeled as a historical audit of superseded values and is not a clinically valid sensitivity analysis.

title: Construction of the comparative cohort and site-reviewed case series
verification: canonical numerical checks and publication display checks
caption: Panel A shows the master cohort through supported-product, first-eligible-BCMA/all-talquetamab, bridging, and recorded-ascertainment rules, followed by documented suspected flare and no documented flare groups. Panel B shows the independently reviewed case-series population, confidence assessments, and comparative eligibility exclusions. Bridging and repeat BCMA courses contribute to the descriptive case series when site reviewed but do not enter the primary comparative cohort.

title: Onset and recorded clinical chronology
verification: canonical numerical checks and publication display checks
caption: Panel A shows the empirical cumulative distribution among cases with point onset timing. Panel B uses neutral case rows to show onset, recorded peak, and recorded symptom-resolution days after first step-up dosing. Open markers indicate estimated dates; an onset interval is drawn as an interval without an inferred midpoint. Markers beyond day 100 are placed at the right boundary with a greater-than mark; elapsed values are supplied in Table S1. A missing resolution date does not imply persistent flare. Confidence and bridging status are shown separately.

title: Clinical manifestations impact and index anatomy
verification: canonical numerical checks and publication display checks
caption: Panels A-C describe six manifestation domains, clinical complications and flare-attributed admission, and index anatomical involvement. Domains overlap, and each uses the complete site-reviewed denominator with Yes, No, Unknown, and Not applicable categories. Unknown and Not applicable are separate states. Labels give the Yes count over the total case-series denominator. True extramedullary disease is distinguished from paraskeletal involvement. Spinal and CNS involvement are separate overlapping descriptors; spinal involvement does not by itself imply CNS disease.

title: Exploratory associations with suspected flare response and survival
verification: canonical numerical checks and publication display checks
caption: Panel A shows six independent Firth logistic baseline models for documented suspected flare. Panel B shows adjusted best-response thresholds, and panel C shows adjusted time-dependent PFS and OS associations. Each row provides its estimate, 95% confidence interval, and actual analysis population. Baseline ORs, response ORs, and survival HRs have different outcomes and are displayed separately. Six-covariate adjustment includes age, sex, ECOG performance status, prior treatment lines, high-risk cytogenetics, and true extramedullary disease. Sparse events, missing covariates, post-treatment classification, and wide intervals limit inference; absence of a clear association does not establish equivalence.

title: Proposed clinical recognition and reassessment framework
verification: canonical numerical checks and publication display checks
caption: The proposed framework prioritizes urgent complications, competing explanations, and integration of clinical, biochemical, and imaging evidence. Treatment decisions are individualized rather than determined by a mandatory continuation rule. Longitudinal reassessment records symptom recovery, local lesion outcome, and systemic response separately. This framework is derived from the cohort and literature and has not undergone formal consensus validation or prospective diagnostic evaluation.

title: Landmark progression-free and overall survival
verification: canonical numerical checks and publication display checks
caption: PFS and OS are shown at day-30 and day-60 landmarks with 95% confidence bands and numbers at risk. Follow-up restarts at the landmark. Flare exposure is defined only by onset on or before that landmark; courses developing flare later remain in the no-flare-by-landmark group for that analysis. Patients must be alive and, for PFS, progression-free at the landmark. These descriptive curves condition on landmark eligibility and do not replace the time-dependent primary models.
